title: Language Exposure Matters: Distribution and Order in Multilingual BabyLM Pre-training
abstract: arXiv:2610.20102v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We investigate two aspects of multilingual pre-training with limited data, namely how language exposure is distributed across English, Dutch, and Chinese, and how that exposure is ordered during training. In particular, we compare balanced multilingual exposure to language-dominant exposure, where one language is exposed with more training data than the others. We also compare mixed training, where multilingual training data is used throughout training, with curriculum training, where monolingual exposure of the dominant language is followed by balanced multilingual exposure. Our results show that multilingual BabyLM performance varies with both the amount and order of language exposure. Mixed training outperforms curriculum learning across all 15 matched configurations, indicating that simultaneous multilingual exposure is more effective than staged exposure in our setting. translated_title: 语言暴露至关重要：多语言BabyLM预训练中的分布与顺序
translated_abstract: 我们研究了在数据有限条件下多语言预训练的两个方面，即语言暴露如何在英语、荷兰语和中文之间分布，以及在训练过程中语言暴露的顺序安排。特别地，我们比较了平衡的多语言暴露与语言主导型暴露（即某一种语言的训练数据多于其他语言）。我们还比较了混合训练（在整个训练过程中持续使用多语言训练数据）与课程训练（先进行主导语言的单语暴露，随后进行平衡的多语言暴露）。我们的结果表明，多语言BabyLM的性能随语言暴露的数量和顺序而变化。在全部15个匹配配置中，混合训练均优于课程学习，这表明在我们的设置下，同步的多语言暴露比分阶段暴露更为有效。若干语言主导型的混合训练配置取得了（摘要在此处不完整）
tldr: 在数据有限的多语言BabyLM预训练中，语言暴露的数量与顺序均会影响性能，且全程混合的同步多语言训练在所有15个配置中都优于先单语后多语的课程式训练。
en_tdlr: In data-limited multilingual BabyLM pre-training, both the amount and order of language exposure affect performance, and mixed training with simultaneous multilingual exposure outperforms curriculum learning across all 15 matched configurations.
